bullets.title: NVDA: Broad selloff deepens; Jefferies cuts PT to $250, regulatory/capex concerns dominate
bullets.body: Jefferies' Blayne Curtis cut NVDA PT to $250 citing hyperscaler capex concerns for 2028, while NVDA extended a 6-day losing streak (-3.3% premarket). Key overhangs: California AG subpoenaing over China chip shipments, Commerce Dept approved ~880k Nvidia/AMD AI chips to some Chinese military-linked entities, and China tech (Tencent) flagging potential 2027 capex peak. JPM MI tactically bullish on AI rebound but notes semis HF net exposure down 67% from YTD peak — longest 6-week selling streak on record.

bullets.title: Semis sector rout: AMD -6.5%, MU -5%, MRVL -5.3%, LITE -6.2% on China export curbs + capex fears
bullets.body: Broad semiconductor selloff accelerates premarket: AMD -6.5% (Hunterbrook short report on China business reliance; Commerce approved 879k chips to Chinese military-linked entities), MU -5.0%, STX -5.2%, MRVL -5.3%, COHR -5.9%, LITE -6.2%, ALAB -4.7%. TSMC/Samsung pausing consumer chip shipments to China at 16nm and below; SOX approaching multi-year valuation lows with TD Combo Buy signals near trigger at 73% of constituents.

bullets.title: INTU: Cuts FY27 guidance on Credit Karma AI headwinds; sells Mailchimp for $3.68B; PT cuts across Street
bullets.body: INTU beat F1Q27 (rev $4.35B +1.2% vs consensus; EPS $2.91 +18%) but sharply cut FY27 Credit Karma growth outlook to 3-7% from 11-13%, citing faster-than-expected shift to AI-powered consumer discovery and higher rates. Mailchimp sold for $3.68B (~70% discount to $12B purchase price), proceeds to fund buybacks. KeyBanc cuts PT to $375 from $400 (maintains OW); Piper underweight thesis partially plays out; stock down ~10% premarket.

bullets.title: GOOGL: JPM reiterates OW/$375 PT; Gemini model cadence accelerates, Tasks agent launched
bullets.body: JPM reiterates GOOGL Overweight with $375 Dec-27 PT (22x 2028E GAAP EPS of $17). Three new Gemini 4 models released in <1 month; Neon ranks #3 on Artificial Analysis Index at 32% lower cost than Carbon. Gemini Tasks launched as free AI agent to 1B+ users enabling agentic commerce via AP2/Google Pay. Cloud +103% Y/Y in 3Q with $561B backlog; capacity constraints easing in 2027. Key risk: Search deceleration from +12% Y/Y Q3 to potentially single digits Q4 as AI Overviews cannibalize revenue; RDDT down -60% YTD as a casualty.

bullets.title: SNOW & MDB: High-bar previews — SNOW needs 5pt+ beat and GP acceleration; MDB needs 30%+ Atlas growth
bullets.body: JPM flags binary setups ahead of earnings: SNOW Q3 Product Revenue expected ~+43% Y/Y but needs Gross Profit dollar growth acceleration >+20bps QoQ; Q4 guidance bogey +39-40% vs Street at +36%. MDB Q3 Atlas growth must hit +30% Y/Y to reverse negative sentiment — a +29% print would signal zero acceleration and risk a third consecutive miss.

bullets.title: SPOT: CFO signals mid-teens revenue growth through 2030; AI Remix near launch pending artist opt-ins
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight on SPOT with $700 PT (~30x FY28e FCF). CFO at Barca TMT targets mid-teens total revenue growth through 2030 from subscriber growth, pricing, and ad acceleration; gross margin target 35-40% by 2030. AI Remix licensing agreements signed with UMG, Believe, Kobalt; Q1 2027 launch possible pending artist consent. LYV 'Reserve by Spotify' partnership facilitating hundreds of thousands of tickets, expanding to Europe/Australia in 2027.

bullets.title: META: Muse Charm AI device priced at $300 with Verizon 5G bundle; stock -3.5% premarket
bullets.body: META is pricing its compact Muse Charm AI wearable device at $300 bundled with up to 12 months free Verizon 5G. Stock down 3.5% premarket as AI trade broadly reprices on capital and regulatory constraints; Muse shopping use case reaches ~25% of users with $200+ average purchase sizes per JPM e-commerce note.

bullets.title: AAPL: Developing autonomous AI agent for device control; potential competitive threat to META/others
bullets.body: Reports indicate Apple is developing an autonomous AI agent capable of writing code, browsing the web, and controlling apps — pressuring META and other AI platform stocks. RBC notes AAPL agent report as an incremental AI risk weighing on the broader mega-cap TMT complex.

bullets.title: AMZN: PT raised to $310 at Opco on Anthropic stake; JPM top holiday e-commerce pick
bullets.body: Opco raises AMZN PT to $310 (from $285), attributing ~$97/share to ~3.5B Anthropic shares with 15% holding-company discount. JPM projects AMZN 4Q retail revenue +9.7% FXN Y/Y, maintaining ~48% US e-commerce share; names AMZN alongside SHOP as best holiday ideas with US e-commerce expected +10% Y/Y reaching ~27% of adjusted retail sales.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM best holiday idea; driving ~50% of US incremental e-commerce gains, agentic traffic +2.6x Y/Y
bullets.body: JPM projects SHOP 4Q revenue +33% Y/Y FXN and US GMV ex-POS +25% Y/Y, powering ~18% of US e-commerce (+200bps Y/Y). SHOP's agentic AI traffic grew +2.6x Y/Y in 3Q with orders +3.3x and ~64% higher conversion vs organic search. 7th consecutive quarter of 30%+ revenue growth guidance; store count +15% Y/Y 4QTD.

bullets.title: HPE/DELL: Upcoming earnings; HPE expected to beat Q4 on networking/server pricing
bullets.body: HPE reports Mon Nov 23 (consensus EPS $1.28, rev $14.47B); DELL reports Tue Nov 24 (consensus EPS $6.59, rev $49.22B). UBS Tech desk expects HPE to beat Q4 driven by networking and server pricing strength, lifting F'27-28 estimates by 3%; guide expected above consensus. Both stocks down sharply premarket (DELL -5.4%, HPE down in sympathy with semis).

bullets.title: ARM: $2B AGI CPU sales guidance FY27/28; 4x power efficiency target by 2030 at Barcelona conference
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley European semi conference: ARM targeting ~$2B in AGI CPU sales across FY27/28 with firm confidence in data center build-out through CY27. v10 architecture launch expected 2027 with AI compute and security focus; 4x power efficiency improvement targeted by 2030. ARM acknowledges risk of delays post-2027.

bullets.title: BABA: Cloud unit nearing profitability; external revenue +67% Y/Y, margin 14.5% — JPM expects consensus upgrades
bullets.body: Alibaba cloud external recurring revenue grew 67% Y/Y (well above ~50% investor expectations); EBITA margin expanded to 14.5% from ~12%, covering 84% of AI Labs losses and narrowing combined loss to RMB1.7B from RMB8.2B. Mizuho raises BABA PT to $205 (OW). Key question is sustainability of 67% growth and capex discipline vs chip supply constraints; Alibaba shifting to domestic AI chips with rebound expected by 2028.

bullets.title: CRM: Low guidance bar creates F3Q beat potential; rerating requires acceleration evidence per Opco
bullets.body: Opco maintains Outperform on CRM: low guidance bar could drive F3Q beat, but F4Q/FY28 organic growth outlook remains cautious and sustained rerating requires acceleration evidence. ServiceNow separately building AI-powered CRM tool targeting Salesforce customers — adding competitive pressure.

bullets.title: MSFT: RBC Outperform/$640 PT; Ignite announcements reinforce full-stack AI thesis
bullets.body: RBC maintains MSFT Outperform at $640 PT, citing Ignite conference announcements as reinforcing the full-stack AI thesis across cloud, Copilot, and enterprise software. JPM bond desk remains Underweight MSFT credit, noting hyperscalers face aggregate ~$595B FCF funding gap through 2028.

bullets.title: TSLA: HSBC upgrades to Hold from Reduce; stock +2.5% premarket
bullets.body: TSLA upgraded by HSBC to Hold from Reduce, triggering a +2.5% premarket move — the standout positive in an otherwise broadly negative session for tech and growth names.

bullets.title: HOOD: Wolfe adds to Alpha List at 23x 2028E EPS; down ~36% QTD seen as compelling entry
bullets.body: Wolfe Research adds HOOD to its Alpha List, citing compelling valuation at 23x 2028E EPS (low end of 20x-60x historical range) after a ~36% QTD decline. Core trading business fundamentals remain strong; pipeline of revenue-enhancing products intact; competitive and regulatory risks viewed as overblown.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS/HUT/WULF/CORZ: Roth QSG launching survey on miner-to-AI pivot demand
bullets.body: Roth's Quantitative Survey Group is launching a 100-150 respondent enterprise survey on GPU/HPC hosting demand, specifically targeting vendor preferences between pure-play AI hosters (CRWV) and converted bitcoin miners (WULF, CORZ, NBIS, HUT). Survey assesses selection criteria including price, GPU generation, power, uptime, and provider solvency — results expected to be a catalyst for relative positioning.

bullets.title: WSM: Citi cuts PT to $245 from $275; Pottery Barn slowdown + supply chain headwinds, thesis intact
bullets.body: Citi cuts WSM PT to $245 (from $275) on first negative EPS revision in multiple quarters — Pottery Barn comps slowing with unclear acceleration timeline, port congestion extending supply chain headwinds into FY27, and rising fuel/transport costs. Citi models FY27E EPS $10.70 on +4.8% SSS; rating stays Neutral. Opco notes management not providing FY27 guidance and managing Q4 toward midpoint of ranges.

bullets.title: GS Mutual Fund Positioning: Funds added AMD, PLTR, SNDK, WDC; 722bp underweight Mag7; AMZN first overweight since 2016
bullets.body: GS Q3 mutual fund data (453 funds, $3.9T AUM): largest additions to AI infrastructure (AMD, WDC, STX, SNDK) and software (PLTR, SNOW); new overweight basket adds CRM, NET. Funds remain 722bp underweight Mag7 (unchanged in Q3); AMZN is first Mag7 constituent held overweight since 2016. Largest Mag7 reductions in GOOGL and AAPL. Cash at record low 1.1% of assets.
